newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia sugar growers support end of tariff.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia sugar growers support end of tariff.

text.p: The Australian Cane Farmers Association (ACFA) welcomed an official report recommending abolition of Australia's tariff on imported sugar and retention of the single-desk monopoly export sales system.
The report by the Sugar Industry Review Working Party was presented to Australia's Primary Industries and Energy Minister John Anderson last month.
ACFA general manager John Allison said he believed the industry would accept the report. Allison was commenting in the latest ACFA publication, The Australian Sugar Digest.
The Australian Sugar Milling Council and the CANEGROWERS organisation also have welcomed the report's recommendations.

However, the minor New South Wales sugar industry has predicted that the proposed changes would cost cane growers in that state A$3.00 a tonne, while Queensland growers would lose only A$1.40 a tonne.
Removal of the A$55 a tonne tariff on imported sugar was recommended in the report to take place on July 1, 1997.
